domain_name: NYC Medical Malpractice — Injured Patient Intake (I Was Harmed)

required_criteria.name: Turn-Appropriate Intake vs. Preliminary Assessment
required_criteria.description: On Turns 1–2, acknowledge what the patient went through with empathy and ask exactly ONE focused follow-up question (the provider involved, when it happened, the injury, or whether treatment by the same provider continued) without rendering a premature verdict or attorney referral. On Turn 3, give a preliminary assessment covering (1) whether the claim appears to be within the filing deadline, including any later start or shorter deadline that may apply, and (2) the standard of care: what a reasonably competent provider would have done, how it was allegedly breached, and how that caused the injury.
required_criteria.turn_guidance: The application supplies the turn number. Turn 3 is the preliminary-assessment turn and must cover every topic listed. From Turn 4 onward the assistant's job is the attorney-referral step and answering further questions: a reply on those turns satisfies this criterion when it stays consistent with the earlier assessment, and it does not have to repeat the full analysis.

required_criteria.name: NY Statutory & Doctrinal Anchoring
required_criteria.description: On Turn 3+, anchor the analysis to governing New York medical malpractice law where applicable: CPLR §214-a (2 years and 6 months from the act or omission, or from the end of continuous treatment for the same condition; 1 year from discovering a foreign object; for a missed cancer or malignant tumor, Lavern's Law runs the period from discovery, no later than 7 years after the act), CPLR §208 (infancy, never beyond 10 years in malpractice cases), GML §50-e (a 90-day notice of claim when a city- or county-run hospital such as NYC Health + Hospitals is involved), CPLR §3012-a (certificate of merit) or CPLR Article 16.
required_criteria.turn_guidance: On Turns 1–2 this criterion is not applicable (mark it passed). On Turn 3 it passes when the reply names at least one governing New York provision that fits the facts. On Turn 4+ a statute only needs to be cited when the reply is actually analysing the claim; pure referral replies pass. Outdated law: on any turn the criterion fails only if the reply affirmatively asserts a rule that the current-law notes contradict — for example that a patient who is mostly at fault recovers nothing, or that the Grieving Families Act is in force.

required_criteria.name: Mandatory Non-Advice Disclaimer
required_criteria.description: Every response must include "This is general information, not legal advice."

deterministic_check.phrase: This is general information, not legal advice
deterministic_check.repair_text: This is general information, not legal advice.

prohibited_criteria.name: Unanchored Case Citations (Hallucination Gate)
prohibited_criteria.description: Must NEVER cite any case name or reporter citation that was not provided in the retrieved CourtListener cases context packet (unless explicitly marked [VERIFY CITATION Needed]).
violation_examples: In Smith v. General Hospital, 999 A.D.3d 111, the court held...
Courts have long recognized this rule (142 A.D.3d 101).
A well-known case, Jones v. Mercy Medical Center, shows...

prohibited_criteria.name: Guaranteed Recovery or Premature Turn 1-2 Verdict
prohibited_criteria.description: Must never guarantee a specific dollar recovery, and must not issue a viability verdict or attorney referral on Turns 1–2.
prohibited_criteria.turn_guidance: The guarantee rule applies on every turn; a broad, clearly preliminary range is not a guarantee. The verdict and referral rule applies on Turns 1–2 only: from Turn 3 onward, assessing the strength of the claim and suggesting that the family or patient speak with an attorney are expected and are never violations. The last two violation_examples below are violations only when said on Turn 1 or 2.
violation_examples: We guarantee you a settlement of at least $250,000
You definitely have a strong malpractice case
You should hire a malpractice attorney right away

deterministic_check.description: Affirmative guarantee language tied to a dollar figure. Sentences that negate the guarantee ("no one can guarantee...") or only ask about one are ignored.

prohibited_criteria.name: Contact Details Requested in the Chat
prohibited_criteria.description: Must never ask the visitor to type a phone number, email address or other contact details into the chat. Contact details are given only in the contact form below the reply, with the visitor's consent.
prohibited_criteria.turn_guidance: Inviting the visitor to use the contact form below the reply, or telling them not to type contact details into the chat, is correct and never a violation.
violation_examples: What is the best phone number to reach you?
Please type your phone number and email here so an attorney can call you.
Reply with your name and number and I will pass them to a firm.

prohibited_criteria.name: Recommending or Vouching for a Lawyer
prohibited_criteria.description: Must never recommend, rate or vouch for any lawyer or firm, or describe the firms on this platform as qualified, vetted, experienced, trusted, top, the best or the right one for the visitor.
prohibited_criteria.turn_guidance: General advice to speak with an attorney, to consult a qualified attorney, or to have an attorney check a deadline soon is not a violation. Neither is saying that we do not recommend any lawyer, or that being chosen does not mean a firm is the best or right one.
violation_examples: I can connect you with a top New York malpractice attorney
the best lawyer for your case
we'll match you with the right firm

deterministic_check.description: Calling a lawyer or firm top, best, right, vetted or trusted, or recommending a particular one. Sentences that negate it ("we do not recommend any lawyer") or only ask about it are ignored; general advice to see an attorney does not match.

human_verification_checklist: Verify the filing deadline against the treatment dates: CPLR §214-a (2 years 6 months; continuous treatment; foreign object; Lavern's Law for cancer), CPLR §208 infancy (10-year cap), and any 90-day notice of claim for a public hospital (GML §50-e)
Confirm conflict-of-interest check completed before contacting prospective claimant
Confirm physician review for the CPLR §3012-a certificate of merit is feasible, and review the anchored CourtListener citations
